title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — Premium Revision Paper #15

pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word is a definite article? (1 mark)
   A. the
   B. a
   C. some
   D. an

2. What should you do first when you get a form? (1 mark)
   A. Start writing at once
   B. Sign it
   C. Fold it
   D. Read the instructions

3. What is the plural of 'tooth'? (1 mark)
   A. teeths
   B. toothes
   C. teeth
   D. tooths

4. Which plural is irregular? (1 mark)
   A. books
   B. boxes
   C. children
   D. dishes

5. Which part of a composition tells who, where and when? (1 mark)
   A. The title only
   B. The body
   C. The conclusion
   D. The introduction

6. Why did the woman say Neema's mother had taught her good manners? (1 mark)
   A. Because Neema spoke and acted politely
   B. Because Neema was late
   C. Because Neema was tall
   D. Because Neema was rich

7. Which word has a silent h at the start? (1 mark)
   A. hen
   B. hour
   C. hand
   D. house

8. Which describes the letter b? (1 mark)
   A. A stick with the round part on its right
   B. A round part with the stick on its right
   C. A stick that goes below the line
   D. A dot only

9. In which direction does the sun set? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. South
   C. North
   D. East

10. On a map, the four main directions are (1 mark)
   A. up, down, left and right
   B. north, south, east and west
   C. red, blue, green and yellow
   D. front, back, near and far

11. Which word is a pronoun? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. bridge
   C. green
   D. she

12. Pronouns: Which sentence is correct? (1 mark)
   A. The house is ours.
   B. The house is ours'.
   C. The house is ours's.
   D. The house is our's.

13. Which phrase has adjectives in the correct order? (1 mark)
   A. a round red small ball
   B. a red round small ball
   C. a small round red ball
   D. a round small red ball

14. About how long is a Grade 4 narrative composition? (1 mark)
   A. 60 to 80 words
   B. 5 words
   C. 1000 words
   D. 10 words

15. Which sentence usually ends with a falling voice? (1 mark)
   A. Where is the file?
   B. Is the file here?
   C. Did you send it?
   D. Can I use it?

16. Where do you see a reply to your email? (1 mark)
   A. In the inbox
   B. In the keyboard
   C. On the wall
   D. In the outbox

17. 'A lot of' can be used with (1 mark)
   A. only plural nouns
   B. only names
   C. only verbs
   D. both countable and uncountable nouns

18. Which words link one picture to the next? (1 mark)
   A. first, then, at last
   B. big, small, tall
   C. mango, rice, milk
   D. red, blue, green

19. Which of these does NOT need a capital letter? (1 mark)
   A. Christmas
   B. Eid
   C. Madaraka Day
   D. dry season

20. What is a shed on a farm? (1 mark)
   A. A person who works on a farm
   B. A tool for digging
   C. A small building for tools or animals
   D. A kind of crop

21. Which word begins with /v/? (1 mark)
   A. weed
   B. wheat
   C. window
   D. vegetables

22. What is compost made from, according to Mama Neema? (1 mark)
   A. Maize flour
   B. Plastic and stones
   C. Cement and sand
   D. Vegetable peelings and dry leaves

23. Where was Omondi's mother on the day of the story? (1 mark)
   A. At school
   B. At the market
   C. At the clinic getting her medicine
   D. At the barber's

24. Which word in this sentence is the adverb? 'The nurse spoke gently.' (1 mark)
   A. spoke
   B. nurse
   C. The
   D. gently

25. Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Mama, may I go to the shop?
   B. Mama may, I go to the shop?
   C. Mama may I go to the shop.
   D. Mama, may I go to the shop.

26. Where does the comma go? (1 mark)
   A. Yes I will, help.
   B. Yes I will help,
   C. Yes, I will help.
   D. Yes I, will help.

27. What is inferring the meaning of a word? (1 mark)
   A. Working out its meaning from the words around it
   B. Spelling it backwards
   C. Ignoring it
   D. Copying it

28. Which sentence is joined correctly? (1 mark)
   A. We swept the floor, nor we wiped the desks.
   B. We swept the floor, yet we wiped the desks.
   C. We swept the floor, and we wiped the desks.
   D. We swept the floor, for we wiped the desks.

29. Which sentence has the /ð/ sound in the first word? (1 mark)
   A. Thank the coach.
   B. The team practised hard.
   C. Think before you act.
   D. Three players scored.

30. What is at the centre of a mind map? (1 mark)
   A. The main topic
   B. The author's name
   C. The date
   D. The last idea

31. Which question is correct for asking about the owner of some boots? (1 mark)
   A. Whose is these boots?
   B. Who boots are these?
   C. Whose boots are these?
   D. Whose are boot these?

32. Which word begins with the cluster 'pr'? (1 mark)
   A. protect
   B. brush
   C. clap
   D. grow

33. Which word begins with the cluster 'br'? (1 mark)
   A. clap
   B. grass
   C. broom
   D. sweep

34. Which sentence uses the correct participle of 'eat'? (1 mark)
   A. She has eaten her lunch.
   B. She have eaten her lunch.
   C. She has ate her lunch.
   D. She has eating her lunch.

35. What is the past participle of 'write'? (1 mark)
   A. writed
   B. written
   C. writing
   D. wrote

36. Which tense do we usually use for earlier events in a diary? (1 mark)
   A. Past tense
   B. Command
   C. Future tense
   D. Question form

37. What is a fine? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of salary
   B. A payment for a service
   C. Money paid as a punishment for breaking a rule
   D. A gift of money

38. How do newspapers and magazines usually differ? (1 mark)
   A. Magazines have no pictures
   B. They are the same
   C. Newspapers give news often; magazines give features less often with more pictures
   D. Newspapers have no words

39. What does 'skimming' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading backwards
   B. Copying a passage
   C. Looking for one number
   D. Reading quickly to get the main idea

40. Which sentence uses the correct preposition for a public vehicle? (1 mark)
   A. He is by the bus in.
   B. He is on the bus.
   C. He is at the bus inside.
   D. He is in the bus.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write two reasons why people keep diaries. (2 marks)

42. Put in order: Baraka presses Send; Achieng explains what an email is; they click Compose. (3 marks)

43. Explain the difference in position of 'enough' with a noun and with an adjective. Give an example of each. (4 marks)

44. Why did the teacher say the prize message might be a trick? (3 marks)

45. Fill in the double letters: di__er, ye__ow, bu__on. (3 marks)

46. Punctuate: 'we planted maize beans and sorghum' (2 marks)

47. Explain when we use some and when we use any. Give an example of each. (4 marks)

48. List three places where we use a capital letter. (3 marks)

49. Tell in three sentences how to set up a reading club. (3 marks)

50. List three steps to follow before writing a pictorial composition. (3 marks)

51. Give the meaning of each word and use it in a sentence: (a) harvest (b) fertilizer. (4 marks)

52. Give two reasons why we must fill in forms carefully. (2 marks)

53. Write a friendly letter of about five sentences to a friend in another school about new road safety words you learnt. (5 marks)

54. Write a short headline and two sentences for a news story about your school. (3 marks)

55. Arrange in order and write as a paragraph: (a) Finally, we went home. (b) We arrived at the farm at nine. (c) Then we fed the goats. (3 marks)

56. Write two polite phrases you could use in a conversation, one to add something and one to give the other person a turn. (2 marks)

57. Explain how to make the sound /r/. (3 marks)

58. State two things you can find in a dictionary entry. (2 marks)

59. State two habits of a good listener. (2 marks)

60. Write two sentences using 'compose' and 'reply'. (2 marks)

61. Write two similes to describe a tractor and a hot day. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — the
   The is the definite article.

2. D — Read the instructions
   Instructions tell you how to fill in the form.

3. C — teeth
   Tooth is irregular.

4. C — children
   Child becomes children, not childs.

5. D — The introduction
   The introduction sets the scene.

6. A — Because Neema spoke and acted politely
   Her actions showed good manners.

7. B — hour
   Hour begins with a vowel sound, so the h is silent.

8. A — A stick with the round part on its right
   For b the stick is on the left and the round part on the right.

9. A — West
   The sun sets in the west.

10. B — north, south, east and west
   These are called the cardinal points.

11. D — she
   She takes the place of a noun.

12. A — The house is ours.
   Possessive pronouns are written without an apostrophe.

13. C — a small round red ball
   The order is size, shape, colour.

14. A — 60 to 80 words
   The design asks for about 60 to 80 words.

15. A — Where is the file?
   WH questions usually fall.

16. A — In the inbox
   Received messages are kept in the inbox.

17. D — both countable and uncountable nouns
   For example a lot of books and a lot of rain.

18. A — first, then, at last
   They are linking words for order.

19. D — dry season
   Seasons are common nouns and take small letters.

20. C — A small building for tools or animals
   A shed is used for storing tools or sheltering animals.

21. D — vegetables
   'Vegetables' begins with /v/, said with the top teeth on the lower lip.

22. D — Vegetable peelings and dry leaves
   Compost heaps are made of peelings and dry leaves.

23. C — At the clinic getting her medicine
   The story says she was at the clinic.

24. D — gently
   'Gently' tells how she spoke.

25. A — Mama, may I go to the shop?
   A comma after the person addressed, and a question mark at the end.

26. C — Yes, I will help.
   A comma follows 'Yes'.

27. A — Working out its meaning from the words around it
   Context gives clues.

28. C — We swept the floor, and we wiped the desks.
   'And' adds an idea.

29. B — The team practised hard.
   'The' has voiced 'th'; 'think', 'three' and 'thank' have unvoiced 'th'.

30. A — The main topic
   The main topic is in the middle.

31. C — Whose boots are these?
   'Whose' is followed by a noun.

32. A — protect
   'Protect' begins with p and r.

33. C — broom
   'Broom' begins with b and r.

34. A — She has eaten her lunch.
   Has + eaten.

35. B — written
   Write, wrote, written.

36. A — Past tense
   Events that already happened use the past tense.

37. C — Money paid as a punishment for breaking a rule
   Fines punish law breaking.

38. C — Newspapers give news often; magazines give features less often with more pictures
   Newspapers are published often and carry news.

39. D — Reading quickly to get the main idea
   Skimming gives the gist.

40. B — He is on the bus.
   We say 'on the bus'.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: To remember events; to practise writing; to record feelings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Achieng explains what an email is; they click Compose; Baraka presses Send.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct position.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: With a noun, enough comes before it: enough food. With an adjective, enough comes after it: tall enough.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each position and 1 mark for each example.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: It promised a prize but asked for personal details, and some people send such messages to steal information.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for prize, 1 mark for details, 1 mark for stealing.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: dinner, yellow, button
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: We planted maize, beans and sorghum.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each comma and capital/full stop.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Some is used in positive sentences and polite offers: I have some books. Any is used in questions and negatives: Do you have any books?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule and 1 mark for each example.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: The first word of a sentence; the word I; names of people; names of places; days and months (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Agree on a regular time and a quiet place. Each member reads a book they have chosen. Take turns to tell the group about it and keep a list of the books read.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible sentence.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Look at all the pictures, put them in order, ask who, where and what, make notes, think of a title.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: (a) Harvest: to gather crops that are ready. We harvest maize in August. (b) Fertilizer: something added to soil to help plants grow. The farmer put fertilizer on the field.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each word: 1 for the meaning and 1 for a correct sentence.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: The reader depends on the information, so a mistake may cause confusion or lost messages. Wrong information may delay help.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: A letter with address and date, Dear ..., a body that mentions words such as roundabout, foot bridge and railway crossing, a closing and a name.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for address and date, 1 for greeting, 1 for body content, 1 for closing and name, 1 for punctuation.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Headline: Pupils Win Football Match. The school team won 2 to 1 on Friday. The pupils were happy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a headline and 1 for each sentence.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: We arrived at the farm at nine. Then we fed the goats. Finally, we went home.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sentence in the correct place.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: 'May I add something?' and 'What do you think?'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable polite phrase.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pull the tongue back a little and curl the tip up without touching the roof of the mouth, and round the lips slightly. The tongue tip touches nothing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for tongue pulled back, 1 mark for the tip not touching, 1 mark for rounded lips.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two: spelling, meaning, part of speech, example sentence, pronunciation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look at the speaker and keep quiet until the speaker has finished a whole idea. Nodding to show you follow is also correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct habit.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: I will compose an email to my uncle. He will reply tomorrow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: The tractor roared like a lion. The day was as hot as a burning coal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable simile.
